rules.description: Bounded rule set (§14.9 BPA policy-node cap, pinned at 256 pending registry freeze). Rule order is not semantically significant (deny-wins is order-free); canonical form sorts rules by JCS bytes.

effect.description: §10.5: a selector is a bounded union of positive (allow) atoms plus explicit deny atoms; deny wins.

rule.description: One rule: a conjunction over the constrained domains. A rule matches a request when every constrained domain's request value is a member of the domain atom (allow rules require the request value to be present; deny rules conservatively match an absent request value — fail closed).

atoms.description: The closed twelve-domain atom table of §10.5, one optional constraint per domain. An omitted domain is unconstrained (top); an empty object is the universal rule. Unknown keys fail closed (additionalProperties false).

atomOperation.description: §10.5 operation row: 'Versioned BPP operation id; subset is set inclusion.' The atom is an explicit finite id set; an empty set matches nothing.

atomObject.description: §10.5 object/resource row: 'Exact source-qualified object id or server-expanded immutable collection snapshot; no mutable alias.' The AST carries only exact source-qualified ids; a pinned collection snapshot is server-expanded to exact ids at preparation with its transform id in the PreparationTrace (§10.5), so no mutable alias or unexpanded reference ever reaches the algebra. Subset is set inclusion.

atomPath.description: §10.5 path row: 'Unicode-normalized logical path segments relative to an exact WorkspaceAllocation root plus exact or subtree; string comparison never authorizes a filesystem open' (the owning broker enforces openat2-equivalent semantics at use). root is the exact WorkspaceAllocation ref; segments are NFC-normalized (evaluator-checked), never '.', '..', '/', or control characters. Different roots are disjoint. subtree covers the node and everything beneath it; exact covers only the node.

atomNetworkDestination.description: §10.5 network destination row: 'Scheme, A-label hostname or normalized IP/CIDR, port/range, and protocol; DNS resolution is pinned by the broker and private/special ranges require explicit atoms.' A DNS host and an IP/CIDR host are incomparable at policy level (the algebra never resolves names — typed reject); ip4 and ip6 forms are decidably disjoint. A CIDR with nonzero host bits below the prefix is not normalized and fails closed (evaluator-checked).

atomBinding.description: §10.5 provider/region/recipient row: 'Source-qualified immutable binding id; display names have no policy role.' Explicit finite set of exact binding ids; subset is set inclusion.

atomPurpose.description: §10.5 purpose row: 'Exact purpose ref or descendant in a pinned acyclic purpose snapshot.' snapshot pins the exact acyclic purpose snapshot (typed DigestRef); path is the materialized root-to-node ancestor chain from that snapshot (verified against the pin at preparation), so descendant testing is pure path-prefix comparison — no resolution inside the algebra. The atom covers the named node and its descendants; atoms over different snapshots are incomparable (typed reject).

atomClassification.description: §10.5 classification row: 'Element of a pinned finite lattice; restriction order is the lattice order.' lattice pins the exact finite lattice (typed DigestRef); allowed is the explicit downward-closed element set expanded against the pin at preparation (finite because the lattice is), so the lattice order is absorbed into set inclusion: subset is allowed ⊆ allowed, intersection is set intersection. Atoms over different lattices are incomparable (typed reject; §10.2 incomparable classification blocks derivation).

atomTime.description: §10.5 time row: 'Closed UTC server-time interval; a child interval must be contained.' Integer milliseconds of authoritative server time (§10.5: deadlines and expiry use authoritative server time); both endpoints inclusive; not_before <= not_after (evaluator-checked).

atomQuantity.description: §10.5 quantity row: 'Non-negative fixed-scale integer plus dimension and canonical unit; money additionally names ISO currency and pricing revision.' The atom is a ceiling: it covers integer amounts 0..max at the named fixed scale. Atoms differing in dimension, canonical_unit, scale, currency, or pricing_revision are incomparable (typed reject — §10.5: currency conversion and floating-point quantities reject); subset is max <= max; intersection is min(max).

atomRate.description: §10.5 rate row: 'Exact integer token-bucket RateCeiling and authority-server epoch; subset uses capacity/refill/burst containment.' Fields verbatim from the §10.5 RateCeiling record (integer discrete refill; clock is always authority_server). Atoms differing in dimension, canonical_unit, or epoch are incomparable (typed reject). Subset is the §10.5 containment: capacity <= capacity, max_burst <= max_burst, and refill-rate containment by exact integer cross-multiplication (child.refill_amount * parent.refill_period_milliseconds <= parent.refill_amount * child.refill_period_milliseconds — no floats). Worst-case boundary-alignment dominance beyond this containment is enforced at consume time by atomic ancestor-counter locking (§10.5) — ADR-0001 open item.

atomAssurance.description: §10.5 assurance row: 'Element of a pinned finite refinement order; incomparable profiles reject.' order pins the exact finite refinement order (typed DigestRef); admitted is the explicit upward-closed profile set expanded against the pin at preparation, so the refinement order is absorbed into set inclusion. Atoms over different orders are incomparable (typed reject); within one pinned order, profile-level incomparability is absorbed by the explicit-set expansion.

atomSchemaEvidence.description: §10.5 schema/evidence row: 'Exact immutable schema, verifier, attestor, and assurance-policy digests.' One exact digest tuple per atom (alternatives are separate rules); subset and intersection are exact tuple equality.

requestAtoms.description: The request side of decide(policy, request_atoms): one concrete value per supplied domain, compiled by the kernel from the dependency closure (§10.6), never caller-shaped. purpose reuses the atom shape (exact node = root-to-node path in the pinned snapshot); rate is the requested RateCeiling (matched by containment); schema_evidence is the exact offered digest tuple. An allow rule requires the constrained domain to be present and matching; a deny rule conservatively matches an absent domain (fail closed).

bpa1Policy.description: A BPA-1 policy value is a bounded set of rules; each rule is {effect: allow|deny, atoms} where atoms constrains a subset of the twelve closed §10.5 domains (an omitted domain is unconstrained; an empty atoms object is the universal rule). Free text, regexes, shell syntax, display names, floats, mutable aliases, and implementation callbacks are not policy values (§10.5); all quantities are fixed-scale I-JSON safe integers. Canonical form (evaluator-enforced, policy/eval.py + policy/eval.mjs): set members sorted by UTF-16 code units, rules sorted by their JCS bytes, duplicates rejected; canonical bytes are RFC 8785 JCS and the policy digest is derived over the $domain-tagged canonical form with digest domain bpa1-policy-v1 (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §2, D-R0-1; the DigestRef class is chosen by the embedding record per §14.2). This schema is $domain-safe: every object is closed (additionalProperties false) and no property is named $domain. Cross-field rules JSON Schema cannot express are evaluator-checked and vector-pinned (spec/vectors/policy/): not_before <= not_after, ports.first <= ports.last, CIDR host bits zero below the prefix, NFC-normalized path segments, no duplicate set members. Bounds follow §14.9 (256 list items, 128-byte identifiers, bounded depth); the registry may re-pin them at bundle freeze.

portableBindingDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.2 cross-boundary class rule, amendment §A8; RT-02): this field commits to a FROZEN cross-boundary fragment the consumer holds and must re-derive without a byom secret, so exactly class portable_public (unkeyed SHA-256 over the $domain-tagged canonical fragment) is acceptable. A well-constructed digest of any other class here is digest_class_mismatch — and a keyed one would be a value the consumer could only echo, which is the defect the rule exists to prevent.
